newsitem.title: USA: Yellen says not satisfied with 2.5 pct U.S. growth.
newsitem.headline: Yellen says not satisfied with 2.5 pct U.S. growth.

text.p: The United States should strive to do better than a growth rate of 2.5 percent, Janet Yellen, President Clinton's nominee as chairwoman of the Council of Economic Advisers, said Wednesday.
She said she advocated pursuing policies that would boost growth through increased productivity.
"I consider it a very important priority," Yellen, who is currently a Federal Reserve governor, told the Senate Banking Committee at her confirmation hearing.
Asked about her views on a proposal to amend the constitution to require a balanced budget, she said she was "strongly opposed" to the idea.

"I am very concerned that a balanced amendment would have adverse effects," Yellen said, citing the possibility of extreme circumstances, such as an economic shock, in which it might be preferable to run a deficit for a short period of time.
She did say, however, that at the present time she viewed a balanced budget as an "extremely desirable" goal.
Regarding taxes, Yellen said she did not see a need for increases at this point to balance the budget and said she favored targeted tax cuts.
Asked whether she would favor broad-based capital gains tax cuts, Yellen responded, "I would not regard it as a high priority at this time."
